newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Merpati plans Hong Kong link from next month.
newsitem.headline: Merpati plans Hong Kong link from next month.

text.p: Indonesian airline Merpati Nusantara plans to start a new route between Jakarta and Hong Kong next month, the airline's public relations director told Reuters.

In a telephone interview from Merpati's headquarters in Jakarta, A. Tondo Widodo said the airline was awaiting the arrival of two Airbus A300-600 aircraft on lease before the three times a week service could begin. He could not give an exact start date and said the flight might stop in Medan en route to and from Hong Kong to pick up passengers.
"The main problem is waiting on the aircraft to arrive but we hope to start the Hong Kong service next month. Plans are in the final stages," he said.

Merpati face competition on the Jakarta route from three airlines offering direct services. Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd says it offers 12 flights a week, Garuda has daily connections and China Airlines (CAL) twice a week.

Up to now, Merpati has been known as the domestic subsidiary of flag carrier Garuda Indonesia but industry observers said it is being split from its parent in preparation for privatisation and has been granted permission by the Indonesian government to fly international services in competition with Garuda.

Merpati says it recently started started flying from Jakarta to Melbourne in Australia using its first widebodied aircraft, a newly acquired Airbus A310 which is also being used for daily domestic services to Medan.
